key_insight: The paper shows that tensor-network compression of Fourier pricing can replace memory-heavy FFTs for large European option grids while preserving accuracy.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable path for computational finance workflows that need fine discretization but cannot afford the exponential memory footprint of classical Fourier operators.
method: Reformulate Carr-Madan option pricing in a tensorized form.
Apply the Superfast Fourier Transform (SFFT), a compressed Tensor Train representation of the QFT.
Compare classical tensor-network pricing with QFT-based simulations on quantum simulators and hardware.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on European call options showing maintained pricing accuracy, reduced memory use, and subexponential scaling versus conventional FFT-based pricing.
watch_item: Performance depends on successful tensor compression and practical hardware/simulator constraints, so gains may diminish if the option grid or tensor structure is poorly suited to low-rank representation.
paper_title: Classical Tensor Network and Quantum Fourier Transform Approaches for Large-Scale Carr-Madan Option Pricing
